completed_private_progress.proved_scope: A high-filtration absolute boundary gives the exact lambda divisibility needed to lift the prescribed source through a higher quotient; its unchanged first label is therefore a classical cycle. This proves the reverse survival implication, not the final differential target comparison.
The absolute quotient boundary and its strict naturality square are proved for the prescribed quotient and suspension maps. Commutativity does not supply a crossing conclusion.

The forward classical-differential to absolute lambda-quotient boundary comparison is proved with actual representatives, lambda powers, filtrations and infinity labels. Reverse proves the complementary differential comparison; CrossingDelta and CrossingShift now prove the complete classical delta no-crossing conversion.

Finite induction on actual filtrations proves representative correction and four-edge synchronization under TowerNoCrossing. The new converse construction turns same-source-grade, higher-target-filtration corrections into the full actual TowerNoCrossing condition. The delta crossing premise is now supplied by CrossingDelta and CrossingShift; the general finite/infinite f conversion remains separate.

Actual finite and infinite E-infinity windows identify classical labels and precisely characterize nonzero lambda images by the paper boundary exclusion. No strict extension-lifting assertion is made.

A finite essential extension has source displacement less than the quotient exponent. Consequently the actual page-two extension map has no higher-source crossings; the general conversion remains pending. The additional minimal-length exclusion is proved in CrossingFinite.

For a specified finite-quotient representative, its first label and absolute boundary detection imply the actual classical differential. Adjacent-lift ambiguity is controlled modulo the actual boundary group. GL2 now uses this result; construction of its synchronized representative remains pending.

The finite filtration window and quotient-triangle exactness give strict source lambda division. The prescribed lambda and absolute boundary maps form a proved square up to an explicit target isomorphism, with two-way filtration transport. These results now support the complete delta no-crossing conversion in CrossingDelta; they do not assert compatible division of an arbitrary f-extension relation.

Strict lambda division of an actual finite normalized-map source and filtration of its image are proved in the fixed quotient. They exclude higher-source essential crossings in the minimal normalized-length range m <= e(f). In the range m <= e(f)+1, every possible crossing has u=s+1, v=s+e(f)+1 and m=e(f)+1. This position constraint does not prove the next-length no-crossing conversion or the general finite f conversion.

The complete classical NoCrossingOn to actual absolute-boundary TowerNoCrossing implication is proved with no added hypotheses. Strict source lambda division, the reverse survival comparison, BHS differential existence and a zero-target forward boundary representative produce the required same-source-grade correction.

The complete absolute-boundary no-crossing implication is transported to every vertical shift of nu X, including the normalized source object. The quotient/shift comparison retains its actual projection square and proves filtration compatibility for the fixed boundary map.

Actual finite lambda division is constructed from the detected source, uniformly including exponent zero. The divided representative has source label congruent to the original label modulo a boundary, and the resulting classical differential is invariant under this ambiguity. The unified reverse wrapper requires only the actual lambda equation and the specified divided boundary detection; it chooses the first label internally.

The actual rho lift preserves detection of the original label, via finite filtration reflection and injectivity on E-infinity. Later cycles follow from the higher finite window. GL1 uses the resulting weighted right-edge survival theorem.

The complete infinite normalized-map extension equation is pushed through the actual lambda power and absolute-boundary suspension, retaining both actual source and target infinity classes and their transported E2 representatives. This is a forward propagation only; no-crossing preservation and comparison with the specified left-edge class remain separate.

The fixed sphere first quotient is identified with the additive group ZMod 2 using the registered actual sphere coordinates and archive_dimension(0,0). Every sphere automorphism acts trivially after Q1. Actual quotient-shift and quotient-map naturality extend this to every bigraded sphere and arbitrary synthetic target. This does not assert that unquotiented homotopy groups have characteristic two.

The actual boundaries before and after finite lambda division have strictly equal Q1 labels. The difference between the selected exact shift comparison and canonical suspension is a natural automorphism of the represented homotopy functor. Yoneda identifies its action with a sphere automorphism, whose Q1 action is proved trivial. No global equality of the two shift comparisons is assumed.

The weighted absolute-boundary detection is converted into the classical differential. A higher rho lift retains source detection, actual lambda division gives the correct source modulo boundaries, and the strict Q1 boundary comparison determines the target. The final target ambiguity is contained in the permitted B_k. All zero and endpoint cases are included without a new hypothesis.

The actual quotient/absolute-boundary square is assembled from three TowerExtensionEquation inputs and their no-crossing conditions. One right-edge representative has the specified finite label and its own specified boundary label. Canonical ESS shift transport gives unshifted boundary detection; the GL1 version only requires the top target label and gives high boundary filtration without a bottom label assumption.

The actual finite and infinite extension witnesses supply the top edge and the lambda-propagated bottom edge with all degree transports checked. The private assembly wrappers use the proved bottom target label comparison for GL2. Their remaining inputs are the left-edge label match and crossing conversions.

The actual lambda/shift propagation of the unshifted Y infinity target retains the prescribed classical target label. Positive lambda powers are identified with the registered infinityLambda window map; exponent zero is proved from the actual shift unit and filtered graded comparison. The resulting target label is supplied directly to the GL2 square wrapper without a new local assumption.

completed_private_progress.proved_scope: The HF2 universal-coefficient comparison proves exponent two for classical Adams pages. Negation transports actual detected representatives; actual homotopy groups are not assumed to have exponent two.

Existing actual-quotient exactness and octahedra produce the same restriction lift and a lambda preimage of its second image. The actual normalized triangle and unit relative lambda triangle are also instantiated in May after rotation; may_tensor_common_lift proves both signed tensor equations for the same c. Comparison of this tensor instance with the fixed Q(X) maps and bigraded sphere source is still pending. No arbitrary lambda preimage is identified with the specified ag representative.

The no-return range d <= -j and the normalized-source quotient comparison for exponents at most one are proved using actual filtration vanishing. This extends the existing no-return proof without assuming equality of arbitrary quotient maps.

The given normalized distinguished triangle identifies the cofiber of normalized g with the prescribed shifted nu X. The inclusion and signed boundary equations are proved from the same triangle isomorphism. MH2 transports its existing quotient lift through this isomorphism and proves its strict rho equation; the simultaneous second May equation remains pending.

Quotient restriction maps that agree on the actual inclusion agree after evaluation on spheres in the no-return range. Chosen quotient/shift comparisons therefore preserve the strict restriction equation of the same desuspended representative. MH2 now uses this transport for its prescribed lift in unshifted nu X.

Classical differential no-crossing makes the relative quotient boundary identical for representatives with the same first grade: the absolute-boundary image difference has filtration beyond the complementary finite-quotient window. This handles the differential no-crossing branch of MH2 representative synchronization; the general h-extension branch and simultaneous May image equation remain pending.

Removal of the specified zero vertical shift preserves finiteNuLabel with a=0 as the prescribed finiteTargetLabel, and transports detection along the actual quotient map of shiftZero.hom, for every quotient length and lambda label index. The proof uses the quotient inclusion square and the target-label definition. It does not assert compatibility for positive vertical shift a=1 or for nu.suspensionIso with the classical DesuspendsClass relation.

A chosen octahedron produces a common lift of two prescribed compatible images. The actual finite quotient triangle constructs the same intermediate vertex from aZ and the prescribed ag. Its comparison into the fixed Q_(i+q)(Cg) has the correct restriction on every sphere by the proved finite no-return window bound; its second image is a fixed K evaluated on the prescribed input. The actual identification of that K evaluation with the signed lambda transition remains separate. Both constructions are called by MH2. Two private conditional comparison lemmas factor K-J through the shifted first arrow when delta followed by K equals delta followed by J, and show equality on a prescribed boundary representative. They do not prove this compatibility for the standard May lambda map, and are not yet used to close MH2.

From an actual finite extension witness, positive length implies zero leading E2 image on both the finite quotient and the unquotiented normalized map. A common shift preserves the finite version by actual shifted representatives and filtration. Zero length gives the specified target as the exact finite and unquotiented E2 image. These eleven private lemmas have complete proofs, but do not establish the May K/J comparison, shifted inclusion naturality on nonpermanent labels, h-source first-quotient compatibility, or the final MH2 boundary-controlled division; the main MH2 proof does not yet call them.
